sections.hypothesis: After a 3.5% rebound confirms a swing low on hourly ETH or BTC, price tends to continue up: a long with a stop 1.5% below and a target 3% above the confirming close has positive expectancy after costs, without any regime filter.
sections.rationale: From backlog S2, version C, the only S2 version with results. Those results don't count: the HMM was fitted on the whole sample (its states leak the future), the pivots were probably drawn with a centred window (bars after the pivot confirm it), and the trend filter was chosen as the best of a sweep on the test data. The rebuild spec asks for the pivots first, strictly lagged and long only, before any regime filter is considered. The honest version buys when the rebound is confirmed, not at the low, which turns it into a short-term momentum entry; that is what is tested. If it has no edge on its own, an HMM filter is unlikely to rescue it, and adding one would be a new trial.
sections.rules: 1h bars. Zigzag with a 3.5% threshold: while falling, track the running low; a pivot low is confirmed when a bar closes at least 3.5% above it, and that close is the signal (buy at the next open). Then track the running high until a close at least 3.5% below it confirms a pivot high, and search for the next low. Stop 1.5% below the signal close, target 3% above it; if a bar reaches both, the stop counts first. One position at a time; risk 1% per trade (kestrel.toml). Long only, spot.
sections.falsification: ETHUSDT 1h and BTCUSDT 1h, 2020-01 to 2025-10 (before the holdout), default parameters, run once each. Reject if, pooled across both markets: net expectancy after costs is 0R or below; or P(expectancy > 0) is under 90%; or fewer than 50 trades.
sections.parameters: swing_bps 350, stop_bps 150, target_bps 300 (the original's values). Only the defaults are pre-registered; the original's swing scaling by regime (1.15x in trend, 0.85x in consolidation) is not part of this test.
sections.costs: A 22 bps round trip against a 1.5% stop is about 0.15R per trade, a heavy hurdle: after costs a win is about +1.6R and a loss about -1.15R, so the win rate has to exceed roughly 42% just to break even. Swings of 3.5% are common on 1h crypto, so expect many trades (perhaps 100-300 a year per market), which makes the sample large but the costs material.
